execution_policy.network_enforcement: reviewed command allowlist plus best-effort dead-proxy and offline environment; this is not an operating-system egress sandbox
execution_policy.environment_injection: known Python, pytest, coverage, Node preload, and upper/lower-case proxy variables are removed before reviewed replacements are set
execution_policy.fallback: fail-closed; a missing required tool or timed-out command fails the gate
execution_policy.dependency_install_note: Dependency resolution is outside this runner. CI installs the reviewed hash-locked requirements-ci.lock before invoking a profile.

fast.description: Portable, deterministic contract checks for every supported CI platform.

full.description: Authoritative offline project verification on the primary Windows/Python environment.

gates.description: Compile Python entry points and source modules to syntax trees without imports, bytecode files, or service calls.
commands: import ast; from pathlib import Path; files=[*Path('src').rglob('*.py'), *Path('scripts').glob('*.py')]; [compile(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'), str(p), 'exec', flags=ast.PyCF_ONLY_AST, dont_inherit=True) for p in files]

gates.description: Ask Node.js to parse every first-party browser module; bundled vendor files are intentionally excluded.
Lock the manifest runner, workflow security posture, pinned actions, and dependency-lock contract.
Verify the already-installed environment has no broken or conflicting distributions.
Run the complete Python regression suite in the repository.
Exercise the deterministic project smoke harness against the checked-in corpus.
Verify the FastAPI surface and all split frontend assets without starting a public server.
Spawn the real stdio MCP server and verify protocol initialization and tool discovery without an LLM call.
Enforce the frozen recommendation baseline, hard constraints, and FASTQ exclusion contract.

Generalization watchdog: run the blind-built held-out query set (eval/eval_queries_holdout.json) against thresholds pinned to its 2026-08-06 first-run baseline. The frozen set remains the only release gate; this gate never loosens it.

Dev-set regression gate: run the R6 dev query set (eval/eval_queries_dev.json, 54 cases covering negation-suffix / disjunction / fastq-colloquial / V(D)J / non-human-model-organism / subtype phenomena). Thresholds = post-fix measurement (Top1/Top5 100.0) floated down slightly to 99.5 — with 49 scored cases a single miss reads 98.0 and goes red; violation/FASTQ pinned at 0.0, NoResult at 5/5. Unlike the held-out watchdog this set MAY be iterated against, so the gate locks the achieved level, not a first-run baseline.

Installer pipeline contract tests: W4 installer contract (tests/test_installer_contract.py), W3 frozen runtime contract (tests/test_frozen_runtime_contract.py), W5 migration and end-to-end contracts (tests/test_migrate_from.py, tests/test_installer_e2e.py). Files are referenced by name; any not yet merged (parallel W4/W5 worktrees) are skipped with a printed note, but when none exist the gate fails closed so the installer surface can never be silently unguarded. Also covered by the pytest-suite gate; this gate makes the installer contract matrix explicit and self-contained.
commands:
import pathlib, sys, pytest
declared = ['tests/test_installer_contract.py', 'tests/test_frozen_runtime_contract.py', 'tests/test_migrate_from.py', 'tests/test_installer_e2e.py']
present = [p for p in declared if pathlib.Path(p).is_file()]
missing = [p for p in declared if p not in present]
if missing:
    print('installer-contracts: in-flight files referenced by name, skipped: ' + ', '.join(missing))
sys.exit(pytest.main(['-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider'] + present))
